messages.subject_clean: dominant frequency overlays - extracting muliple elements
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would like to extract the x and y coordinates for discrete discontinuous elements after performing dfreq() - the dominant frequency overlay.  See http://rug.mnhn.fr/seewave/ and click on the dominant frequency overlay example.  I want to have each of those elements, and then calculate parameters such as start frequency, minimum frequency etc on each element.  If I look at the vectors (see attached example), I can see the x and y values for each element.  But how could I extract each discrete element and have them still associated with the original filename?  I see myself extracting many discrete elements from 1000s of WAV files.

To put it in simpler language - check out the attached plot.  I want to make lots of elements like those (without plotting), and then create several new vectors for measurements on each 'chirp', each associated with the original filename (ie as a vector).

Advice very much appreciated.

Kyle

messages.subject_clean: [seewave] dominant frequency overlays - extracting muliple elements
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kyle,

Well, first you'll have to extract each element, from your attached data, you can see that the y values are NA between elements, so I would use that as your starting point.

You could use a while to get out the elements of interest by jumping from NA to NA, then I would use the plyr package to apply a function to each list of frequencies and save the results in a data frame.

I whipped something up (attached) that may be a good starting point. The while loop is a bit messy but should get the job done. Note that this is assuming that your starting data (a.csv) is perfect and that you've already made sure there are no erroneous elements.

Steffi

messages.subject: Fundamental frequency
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I’m currently working on short continuous sounds (<10s). I would like to extract the fundamental frequency at regular intervals (0.05s ; function fund).

When I get the results, I've many "NA" whatever the value of wl. Indeed, the spectrogram of my sound file indicates "holes" in the fundamental frequency, whereas this isn't the case with an other software (Audacity).

I wonder why I've so many "NA". How or what other function would allow me to recover data from the fundamental frequency at 0.05s intervals?

Hoping that you have solutions to offer me ...

See you soon,

Morgane

You should try to decrease th value of 'fmax'. A try with fmax=800 and threshold=1, seems to be much better, but the function sill returns one NA.

It is true that fund() does not have a 'at' argument, but you a from / to arguments for time focus. Anyway I will add this 'at' thing to the TODO list.

spectro(fichier, ovlp=75, palette=rev.gray.colors.2)
par(new=TRUE)
fund(fichier, fmax=800,type="p",pch=24,ann=FALSE, xaxs="i",yaxs="i",col="black",bg="red",threshold=1)

HTH

Jerome
